title: The Twelve Tables, in this Avalon English, limit gold buried with a corpse
summary: Avalon's Twelve Tables forbid burying gold with a corpse, with an exception for gold dental work.
body: The Avalon English of the Twelve Tables forbids adding gold to a corpse, and then excepts gold dental work. The page dates the tables to 450 BC in its title. The surviving text is a later reconstruction, which the page presents as the laws. The wording on the page includes: "crown is bestowed on him at his burial ... 8. ... Nor gold shall be added to a corpse. But if any one buries or burns a corpse that has gold dental work it shall be without prejudice. 9. It is forbidden ... to build a new pyre or a burning mound nearer than sixty feet to another's building without the owner's consent. 10. It is forbidden to acquire by prescriptive right a vestibule of a sepulcher or a".
